package.description: Lightweight Windows utility to prevent screen locking

en-US.description: Lightweight Windows utility to prevent screen locking
en-US.longDescription:
NoSleep is a lightweight tool that prevents Windows from automatically activating the screen saver, sleep mode, or lock screen. It's designed for situations where you can't change these settings yourself—for example, due to corporate-enforced policies. Inspired by Linux Caffeine.
Windows PowerToys includes a tool called Awake that does the same thing, but PowerToys may require administrator privileges and is quite large. NoSleep aims to be as minimal as possible and runs without any extra permissions.
en-US.name: NoSleep
en-US.releaseNotes:
The lid override and activity simulation are no longer Modern Standby-only:
the tray menu is now gated by what your machine actually has (a lid) rather than by its sleep mode.
New on classic-sleep (S3) machines:
- "Block sleep on lid close" (off by default): the same temporary lid-action override with restore and crash self-healing, previously Modern Standby only. On classic sleep it is a deterministic alternative to away mode.
- "Simulate activity" (off by default): the continuous presence modes — invisible activity or visible mouse movement — now work here too; they keep you looking active rather than adding sleep protection, which classic sleep already fully covers, battery included.
Everywhere:
- Lid-less machines show a disabled "No lid detected" line in place of the lid option, keeping the menu layout identical across devices.
- "Prevent sleep attempts" remains Modern Standby only — away mode already covers every classic sleep trigger, so there is nothing for it to fight.
- Tray menu regrouped: sleep behaviors, app watching, and app lifecycle are now cleanly separated, with the enabled state as the final switch.
- Tooltips reworked in English, Russian and Simplified Chinese: shorter, user-focused, and long ones wrap on multiple lines instead of running off the screen.
Note: the classic-sleep-with-lid combination shares its code path with the verified Modern Standby implementation but was not tested on real S3 laptop hardware.
Still a single executable (net48 build ~250 KB), no new settings keys, dependencies or admin rights; release binaries carry build-provenance attestations.
What's Changed
- Lid override & activity simulation for classic-sleep (S3) machines (1.7.0) by @CHerSun in #21
